title: Practising J. D.'s steps with bottle tops at Five Points
summary: Back to the bottle caps, he practises the steps J. D. gave him on the streets of Five Points and draws curious crowds.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Let's go back to the tap dancing and the bottle caps on your toes, on your feet and what happened with James Walker.

Well, whenever -- like he would tell me, you know, like to do one of his steps or something, he would -- see, my partner was very creative and understanding. He was a creative genius, I think, at that age, because you don't just -- I mean especially a city as large as Atlanta, Georgia, was, man. I mean this is -- although there was only colored people would patronize this 81 Theater, see, but white -- whites used to come there also, you see, because they would have all the most important Negro shows there, you see?

That's all they showed, you know? I mean, you see, moving pictures was white, you know, but that's what happened, you see, by -- so far as the bottle tops are concerned, I mean, whatever my partner, Chuckles J. D., used to teach me, steps or something, I would -- after school I would go up

into a place in Atlanta, Georgia, they called Five Points, five points, you see, and I used to like lick these sounds with the bottom of my bare feet, you see, and I attracted the people walking I would make my feet along the street, you know, and I make these sounds.

And they said, 'Look at him, what's -- they -- what are you doing? What kind of feet is you got?' you know? You know, and I'd do it again, you know, and they could tell -- I was never satisfied until somebody would laugh. I mean they'd actually be -- the laughter would be happening, see.

And -- but they took a liking to me myself because people in the South are thataway, you know. Somebody's child be born, you know, and some neighbors have got the nerve to ask the family, give me that baby. They'd they be serious. They don't be asking to adopt a child. They want to -- like you would give away a puppy or something. You know what I'm saying?
